name: API and Pinterest Tag combined coverage

conditions.detail: For deduplication, the event_id from a browser or app event must match the event_id in the corresponding server event.
If both the API and Pinterest Tag ingest the same event, the event_id must be the same in both instances for Pinterest to regard them as duplicates.
In the case of redundant events, Pinterest retains the first event captured and removes duplicates within 48 hours.
Pass the event_id and event_name parameters in all sources used.
For browser pixel purchase events, send the same order numbers in the eventID parameter as the corresponding server events.
For events without a purchase-related ID, use any random number as long as it is the same for both browser and server events.
event_id can be any unique string associated with the purchase, such as an order number or transaction ID.
If a user makes multiple purchases with distinct order numbers, each API call must include the respective order number as event_id.
event_id is a required string parameter, recommended for all events and all platforms.
event_name is a required string parameter, recommended for all events and all platforms.
event_name must use one of the Pinterest-defined enum values or a custom-defined event name.
Custom event names allow upper- or lower-case letters (case insensitive), numerals 0-9, underscores, and hyphens, limited to 100 characters.
Up to 15 custom event types can be custom-defined per advertiser ID.
Custom events must be mapped to a Pinterest standard event.
Custom events are usable for audience creation.
An incorrectly named event is rejected; the example response shows a 'subscription' event failing with 'Invalid event_name'.
action_source is a required string parameter indicating the platform from which the event was ingested into the API.
action_source accepts the enum values app_android, app_ios, web, and offline.
action_source is different from device_type, which indicates the actual device on which the event occurred.
action_source is recommended for all events on all platforms.
event_time is a required integer Unix timestamp in seconds, recommended for all events.
event_source_url is an optional, nullable string recommended for all web events, containing the full URL path of the conversion event.
For Pinterest click events, event_source_url should include the &epik query string, a unique click identifier.
The epik (External Pinterest ID Key) is a unique identifier Pinterest uses to help track users across devices and sessions, typically passed as a query parameter after a click on a Pinterest ad.
opt_out is an optional boolean indicating whether the user opted out of web or offline conversion events, or enabled Limit Ad Tracking on iOS / opted out of Ads Personalization on Android.
partner_name is an optional, nullable string identifying the third-party responsible for sending the event to the API on behalf of the advertiser.
partner_name syntax is ss-companyname; for direct integration use the value direct.
The parameter tables' recommended/optional tags do not indicate which parameters are required for the API request to succeed; see the Send conversions endpoint reference.
The 'user' in parameter descriptions is the person who took the action that initiated the conversion event.
user_data is a required object that must include at least one of hashed_maids or the pairing of client_ip_address and client_user_agent.
User data parameters are all optional strings nested within the required user_data object.
external_id is a unique string used to identify a customer, such as a user ID or loyalty ID, SHA-256 hashed, recommended for all events on all platforms.
Pinterest uses external_id with other customer information parameters to form an external_id+other-customer-information mapping when an event is matched using customer information parameters.
Having external_id or other customer information helps minimize the impact of matched event data loss when more customer information is restricted from being shared in future events.
Adding more identifiers (external_id) improves event quality and helps improve performance.
Multiple external_id strings can be sent for events in one payload.
Standard external_id strings can be used for all events, such as session ID/visit ID or client ID/visitor ID.
Conditional external_id strings can be used for signed-in users, such as membership ID or loyalty ID.

External cookie IDs are first-party cookie identifiers for a single visit or visitor, set server-side on your own domain, with structure based on your own logic such as browser and device combinations.
External cookie examples include session ID, visit ID, unique visitor ID, client ID, and cookie value.

Your own identifiers (user ID, membership ID, loyalty ID, subscription ID) are generated to manage engagement, performance, and orders for customers, usually stored in your CRM system and updated when a user logs in.
click_id is a cookie generated when a user clicks an ad; use the _epik cookie instead of the &epik= query parameter.
While both _epik cookie and &epik= query parameter are accepted, passing _epik cookie values is necessary when a URL parameter is missing or removed and ensures greater coverage.
click_id is recommended for add_to_cart, checkout, lead, page_visit, search, signup, view_category, and watch_video events.
client_ip_address is the user's IP address, recommended for all web events; valid IPv4 or IPv6, no pure zero (0.0.0.0) addresses.
client_user_agent is the user agent string for the user's browser, recommended for all events; include at least two of OSfamily, browserfamily, devicefamily.
Do not send 'Other' or null user agents, and do not send user agents produced by bots.
country is the SHA-256 hash of a two-character ISO-3166 country code in lower case and UTF format, recommended for all events on all platforms.
ct (city) is SHA-256 hashed in lower case without spaces or punctuation, recommended for all events on all platforms.
db (date of birth) is the SHA-256 hash of YYYYMMDD, recommended for all events on all platforms.
em (email address) is the SHA-256 hash of email addresses in lower case, recommended for all events on all platforms.
ge (gender) is a SHA-256 hash of f (female), m (male), or n (non-binary), recommended for all events on all platforms.
ln (last name) is the SHA-256 hash of the last name in lower case, recommended for all events on all platforms.
ph (phone number) is the SHA-256 hash of phone numbers with only digits, country code, and area code; remove symbols, letters, spaces, and leading zeros.
st (state) is the SHA-256 hash of a two-letter code in lower case, recommended for all events on all platforms.
zp (zip code) is the SHA-256 hash of the zip code with only digits, recommended for all events on all platforms.
hashed_maids are the user's Google Advertising IDs (GAIDs) or Apple's Identifier for Advertisers (IDFAs), SHA-256 hashed, recommended for all app events.
partner_id is a unique identifier for user information, such as RampID, optional for all events and only used by Pinterest integration partners.
App data parameters (app_id, app_name, app_version, device_brand, device_carrier, device_model, device_type, language, os_version, wifi) are optional for all events.
device_type is a free-form string; consider values such as 'desktop web', 'mobile web', 'iPhone app', or 'Android app' (native Pinterest mobile app).
Additional device detail can be provided via app_name, app_version, device_brand, device_carrier, device_model, and os_version.
language is a two-character ISO-639-1 language code in lower case and UTF format.
wifi is a boolean indicating whether the event occurred when the user device was connected to a wireless network.
The optional custom_data object contains event-level information such as money spent in the conversion.
The optional custom_data.contents object contains information about specific merchandise items involved in the event; using it is suggested especially for events involving multiple products.
Product event parameters are all strings (except as noted) and all optional, i.e. not required by the API for the request to succeed.
custom_data.currency is the ISO-4217 currency code used in a purchase event; if not passed, the currency the advertiser set when creating the account is used.
custom_data.value is the total monetary value for purchased items, pre-tax and pre-shipping, accepted as a string and parsed into a double.
Always send currency when sending value; value should not contain unusually high values or invalid values such as negative numbers or zero.
custom_data.content_ids is an array of product IDs related to the event, each also listed in the custom_data.contents array of objects.
custom_data.content_name is the name of the page or product associated with the event.
custom_data.content_category is the type of merchandise; custom_data.content_brand is the brand of merchandise.
custom_data.num_items is the total number of products involved, for example products purchased in a checkout event.
custom_data.order_id is the identifier for the order in a purchase-related event.
custom_data.search_string is the string entered in a search event.
custom_data.opt_out_type is the opt-out type for privacy; the only accepted value is ldp (limited data processing).
custom_data.contents item fields include item_brand, item_category, item_name, item_price (single quantity), quantity, and id.
Batching event data up to the limit of 1000 per request helps make data transfer more efficient and reduces the likelihood of running into rate limits.
Send event data in real time or with a maximum lag time of one hour for better user experience.
Pass actual, real-time values associated with each conversion event rather than static or predetermined values, to ensure data accuracy and integrity for reporting and optimization.
For example, currency for checkouts should reflect the user's currency instead of a universal hardcoded value.
Avoid passing excessively long strings, properly escape special characters using JSON standard guidelines, and separate multiple strings with commas.
Include in the request all parameters recommended for specific platforms and events, and follow the formatting guidelines for all parameters.
The ad_account ID is required for the request path.
The example request sends two events to https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/events with a Bearer token.
The example response shows num_events_received, num_events_processed, and per-event status with error_message and warning_message fields.
An event with an invalid event_name (e.g. 'subscription' instead of 'subscribe') is returned with status 'failed' and an error message.
Tracking conversion events helps measure the success of ad campaigns, optimize marketing strategies, and understand customer behavior.
Conversion events track actions customers take in person or online.
The Conversions API can track events on websites, apps, or offline sources such as store locations.
The Conversions API can be used with Pinterest Tag for additional coverage.
The Conversions API endpoint requires a unique identifier associated with the ad account that is sending events.
A token is needed to authenticate against the Conversions API endpoint: a conversion token for API-only access, or an OAuth token with at least ads:write scopes for other endpoints.
To interact with tools/endpoints related to campaigns, ad groups, and ads, the OAuth token must be related to a Pinterest advertiser ID.
A conversion token is generated in Ads Manager under Ad Account Overview > Conversions > Conversions API > Set up API by selecting Conversion access token and clicking Generate new token.
The generated token is displayed with the ad account ID.
Conversion events are sent via the POST Send conversions endpoint.
Conversion data quality can be checked on the Conversions Health page in Ads Manager.
Event quality in the API can be tracked via the event quality score documentation.
Test events verify that the event payload is constructed correctly for accurate and comprehensive conversion tracking.
Test event data is sent to a sandbox environment and, unlike production data, is not processed for reporting or optimization.
If sending multiple test events in a request, limit the batch to 20 events; only the first 20 events in a batch are processed.
Test events are sent by adding the query parameter test=true to the events endpoint.
Test event delivery is verified in Ads Manager under Campaign manager > Conversions > Test events.

For web events, include the full event_source_url; for Pinterest click events include the &epik query string.

Phone numbers (ph) must be digits only with country code and area code; remove symbols, letters, spaces, and leading zeros.
Country (country) is a SHA-256 hash of a two-character lower-case ISO-3166 code; state (st) is a SHA-256 hash of a two-letter lower-case code.
City (ct) is SHA-256 hashed in lower case without spaces or punctuation; date of birth (db) is SHA-256 hash of YYYYMMDD.

conditions.detail: For Pinterest click events, include the &epik query string in the event_source_url.
The epik value is a unique identifier Pinterest uses to help track users across devices and sessions, typically passed as a query parameter after a click on a Pinterest ad.

Use the _epik cookie (click_id) instead of the &epik= query parameter; while both are accepted, passing _epik cookie values is necessary when a URL parameter is missing or removed and ensures greater coverage.
Batching limit is 1000 events per request.
Pass the event_id and event_name parameters in all sources used, with the event_id identical for each redundant event.
If both the API and Pinterest Tag ingest the same event, the event_id must be the same in both instances for Pinterest to regard them as duplicates.
In the case of redundant events, Pinterest retains the first event captured and removes duplicates within 48 hours.
For deduplication, the eventID from a browser or app event must match the event_id in the corresponding server event.
event_id can be any unique string associated with the purchase, such as an order number or transaction ID.

If a user makes multiple purchases with distinct order numbers, each API call must include the respective order number as event_id, and browser pixel events must send the same order numbers in the eventID parameter.
For events without a purchase-related ID, use any random number as long as it is the same for both browser and server events.

em (email) is the SHA-256 hash of email addresses in lower case; ph (phone) is the SHA-256 hash with only digits, country code, and area code, removing symbols, letters, spaces, and leading zeros.
ge (gender) is a SHA-256 hash of f (female), m (male), or n (non-binary); ln (last name) is the SHA-256 hash of the last name in lower case.
ct (city) is SHA-256 hashed in lower case without spaces or punctuation; db (date of birth) is the SHA-256 hash of YYYYMMDD.
st (state) is the SHA-256 hash of a two-letter code in lower case; zp (zip code) is the SHA-256 hash with only digits.
country is the SHA-256 hash of a two-character ISO-3166 country code in lower case and UTF format.
